query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

per_column.name: spend_tier
per_column.rationale: Bucketing amount into High/Medium/Low gives a genuine grouping axis for expense analysis. It derives from the existing 'amount' column, so it is grounded, though the samples don't expose amount values to fully verify the thresholds; the distribution is plausible.

per_column.name: processing_days
per_column.rationale: Difference between opened_at and processed_date yields a meaningful cycle-time metric for spotting delays. Values align with the dates present, and NULL for the 'nan' processed_date row is correct behaviour.

per_column.name: is_amount_anomaly
per_column.rationale: Flagging outlier amounts is analytically useful for expense audit, giving a targetable subset (12 rows). It is derivable from 'amount', though somewhat redundant with spend_tier and the anomaly criterion is not verifiable from the samples.

per_column.name: fiscal_quarter
per_column.rationale: Quarter labels enable time-based trend grouping, more analytically useful than raw timestamps. Derived from a date; sample values match the processed_date. The 'nan' row was assigned Q4 2023 despite a null date, a minor unsupported inference, but otherwise well grounded.

judge.rationale: All four added columns provide genuine new axes (spend magnitude, cycle time, anomaly flag, temporal bucketing) that support expense analysis rather than trivially restating originals. Values are largely sound readings of the underlying amount and date fields, with correct null handling for silent rows. The one concern is the fiscal_quarter assignment on a row whose processed_date is 'nan', which appears unsupported, and the anomaly/tier thresholds cannot be fully verified from the provided samples. No clear hallucinations observed.
